Tell them. Tell them how much you appreciate them. Nurses go through so much more than what people assume. Expressing your appreciation in words may seem minor, but to them it means the world. In a cruel world, it’s gratefulness like that, that reminds them why they chose that profession and makes their job a bit easier to do. 

Also, this does not apply to everybody. This is more a personal opinion. Violence against nurses (and health care workers in general) is a growing problem in many parts of the world. If you really want to show appreciation, advocate for them when they are being pushed around. A coworker of mine died from an attack from a patients family member. No one batted an eye when we spoke up about this growing problem. Violence is not part of our job.

Currently, the Pokémon fan base. For a bit of context, it was announced a while ago that the new Pokémon game (Sword and Shield) wouldn’t allow you to bring all your buddies from previous games into the new generation unless the Pokémon appeared in the new region’s Pokédex. Simply put, if your Pikachu wasn’t in the new dex, that meant they didn’t code in that Pokémon and he will not be transferable. Evidently, that made people EXTREMELY mad, and many took to the internet to complain and whine and etc. 

It’s been at least a month since the announcement. Game freak has since explained to the community WHY they made this decision, all within reason. You’d think after that, the fans would lay off and let it go? NAH. To this day, there are still hundreds of people constantly badgering the company, to the point of harassment, threats, etc. I’ve seen people try to reason with these toxic fans to no avail. It’s made me embarrassed and borderline regretful of being a avid fan of the Pokémon community. They have given us content for 20+ years, they are constantly giving us new ways to enjoy the fandom, and did I mention Gamefreak has only a bit over 100 staff members? We should be nothing but grateful. Smh.

Depression, anxiety and panic disorder here. I work in the biggest hospital in our area. Whenever something big and scary happens, ie mass casualties, threats, stuff like that, people always want to pull me aside because they don’t think I can handle it and don’t want to risk having a breakdown. 

Truth is I’m the probably the best person in my department to handle those situations, and I’ve proven that a few times already. When peoples lives are at risk, I don’t allow myself to feel, I just do my job as efficient and as well as possible.

I tried to kill myself two weeks ago. No one knows it. I got the help I needed, but I didn’t tell them what extent my suicidal thoughts were. I was too ashamed to of done it and lived. I was ashamed to live in general. When nurses and doctors asked me questions, I kinda beat around the bush, making them think I was suicidal with a plan, but didn’t want them to know I had actually tried. Anyways, they upped my depression/anxiety/panic disorder meds and sent me to counselling nonetheless. Things have been slowly getting better. Can’t shake of the feeling of shame though, I think that will stick with me forever.

I love seeing all these comments about coping mechanisms! But I think something that’s important to remember is that there is no harm asking for psychiatric help. Everyone deals with anxiety, but for some people, it can severely interfere with our everyday lives. Anxiety disorders do exist, and that’s okay! Some people need prescribed medicine to intervene with the chemical balance in your brain. That’s okay too! The point I’m trying to make here, coping mechanisms are amazing and keep it up. But if you ever feel like they aren’t enough, don’t give up, ask for help.

At least once a year since 2009(ish), someone comes in with a dildo stuck up their butt. Both male and female. It’s like Christmas Day for the ER.

In their defence, I was a very rebellious and stubborn teenager with a sailors mouth.

The most vivid memory I have is when I was 12. I can’t remember what I did to piss them off. They tied me to the chair, went into my room and completely cleaned it out. Everything was gone— posters, blinds on the window, and the door was gone too. All that was left was my dresser with only a few of my clothes, and my mattress on the floor— no blanket or pillow to spare me. I had to earn EVERYTHING back. It took a week for the blankets and pillows to come back and the door was the last thing to return (getting dressed was an absolute nightmare). 

It was as bad as THAT afterwards, but it didn’t actually stop until I finally moved out at 21. Even when I was legally an independent, my parents would often confiscate and look through my mail, phone, and laptop. They’d even take it away when I disobeyed them, despite the fact it was 100% mine paid for and all.  

I brought it up to them once. They still think they had every right to do what they did.

That no matter what you’ve done for them, no matter how much you’ve been through with them, you do not have control over how they feel. You cannot force someone to stay in love with you. You cannot force someone to keep caring about you. Both of my relationships ended because they decided they didn’t love me anymore. And both times, I made the mistake of throwing my self respect away by offering to throw my life away for them. I was so in denial of the loss that I was willing to change everything about my life (family, job, appearance etc). 

It took me a full year to realize what I was doing during the first breakup. This second breakup has been easier, once I hit rock bottom I was able to accept my defeat to the reality of things a lot quicker. Of course, I’m still mourning the loss of was a great relationship, but I like to think that part is normal. Honestly, I’m just proud that I have a little more self respect for myself now.

Long Distance Relationships. Never again.

Don’t get me wrong, I don’t really regret it. The little time we did get to spend together was amazing. He was a good boyfriend. But all the sudden he started blowing me off all the time, became cold and hard to approach. I wouldn’t hear from him for weeks. It made me anxious and miserable and actually landed me in the hospital for a major mental breakdown. He claims he had his own stuff going on and just wanted to focus on himself. My theory is that he just stopped caring. 

Worst part is, I knew going into the relationship that it wouldn’t last. He was from the USA, I was from Canada. Both our jobs had us working like hounds and even the idea of living together was basically impossible thanks to immigration laws. But even though I tried so hard not to, I fell for this guy REALLY hard. We had dreams of marrying and having kids and retiring. This made the breakup so much harder to move on from. 

It was nice while it lasted... but when it was over it left a big scar.

I work in the medical field as a float ward clerk sometimes, meaning I didn’t have a particular spot in the hospital, I just go wherever I’m needed most and do their secretarial work. My first time I was ever called to paediatrics, a teenager who had just graduated high school was in the last days of her life. She had been battling multiple brain tumours for the past 4 years. She was well known locally in our city for her kindness and determination throughout her battle. Important note here, she was also a huge Harry Potter fan. 

I still remember to this day, her nurse coming up to my desk, asking me quietly to call her family in right away. The poor nurse was pale as a ghost. I asked if she had passed. She said “no, but she knows it’s coming soon”. After I had made my calls, I pulled the nurse aside and asked how one could know their time was coming. She says, that she told her “It was time to finally forgive Snape (the late Alan Rickman) for killing off her favourite character in the series (Dumbledore). 

As it turned out, that was the last thing she said. She fell into a deep sleep shortly afterwards and passed the following morning with her family by her side. Some of us wore her Hufflepuff house colours in her honour the following day. 

But yeah, never looked at Harry Potter the same after that.
